defects.what: Design-consequence cell says 'the "maximal" system is the marked one; most sample languages grammaticalise a minimal imperative only'. Contradicted by the Map 72A counts printed in the same cell and by my fetch: maximal-only 133, minimal-only 20 (5.3% of 375), both 21, neither 201. The largest class is 'neither'; among languages with a system, maximal-only (133) outnumbers minimal-only (20) 6.65:1. 'Marked' occurs nowhere in chapter 72. The registry S942 row and the entry's own table column state the mapping correctly; only this prose cell is false. Post-lands commit 3f56892f fixed the neighbouring definitions sentence (line 49) but not this cell.

'WALS chapters 72 and 73 explicitly set non-inflectional expressions of the wish aside'. Verbatim true for 73 ('disregards non-inflectional means for expressing the speaker's wish such as (2) and (3)'); false for 72, whose only explicit exclusion is 'negative structures such as (2), which can be called prohibitives (see Chapter 71), fall outside the scope of this chapter', and which in fact admits constructions that 'need not be morphologically or syntactically uniquely imperative-hortative'.

'...Euthykles made me - ... in eleven words': the quoted rendering is eight words; eleven counts only the page's fuller text including the parentheticals '(sc. Smikros)' and '(skulodesph-)' that the entry's own quotation omits.
'six `mined`' - the registry at lands has seven mined rows (S942-S948 are all status mined). Tiers 'six A, one B' are correct.

Prohibitive prose enumerates 113, 182 and 146 and drops 55; '146 use a different verb entirely' is true but incomplete - value 4 also changes the negation strategy. The table above and the registry S944 row ('55 and 146 use another verb form') carry all four cells correctly.

defects.what: Assertions with no support in any of the seven sources: (a) line 25 'the vocative is syntactically outside the clause's argument structure in most languages that have one' and 'the slot accepts apposition without limit' - S945 is a one-sentence glossary entry and carries nothing on argument structure; the S945 registry teaches cell repeats the same overreach ('address is a case or particle slot outside argument structure rather than a mood'); (b) line 33 'Greek and Latin did exactly this with foreign divine names ... epigraphic corpus is full of indeclinable barbarian theonyms'; (c) line 77 'Attested solutions include re-dedication, erasure, legal fiction ..., transfer of the debt to heirs' - 'attested' with no source; (d) line 55 'often a clitic'. These are plausible design-register claims in an entry that declares itself NON-CANON in its section 8, but they are stated as fact without a source.
